# Data map

Every column Idenzy stores, with its classification, purpose and retention.
Derived from the schemas, which are the source of truth (PROJECT.md 4.13.2): the Drizzle
tables in Postgres, and the `analytics.` ones in ClickHouse (ADR-0013).

Idenzy holds no certification. See PROJECT.md 4.13.10 for what is deliberately not done.

## `audit_events`

Data subject: **end_user**, by `actor_id`.

Export only. Erasure must not remove these: the trail keeps the pseudonymous id precisely so an erasure stays provable, which is Art. 17(3)(b) against Art. 17(1).

| Column | Class | Purpose | Retention | In DSR export | Erasure | Encrypted |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | pseudonymous | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | no | retain_pseudonymous | no |
| `actorId` | pseudonymous | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | no | retain_pseudonymous | no |
| `actorType` | pseudonymous | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | no | retain_pseudonymous | no |
| `createdAt` | operational | account_management | until_account_deletion | no | not_applicable | no |
| `entryHash` | pseudonymous | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | no | retain_pseudonymous | no |
| `id` | pseudonymous | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | no | retain_pseudonymous | no |
| `ip` | pii | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | yes | retain_pseudonymous | no |
| `metadata` | pseudonymous | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | no | retain_pseudonymous | no |
| `outboxSeq` | pseudonymous | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | no | retain_pseudonymous | no |
| `prevHash` | pseudonymous | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | no | retain_pseudonymous | no |
| `projectId` | operational | service_configuration | project_lifetime | no | not_applicable | no |
| `seq` | pseudonymous | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | no | retain_pseudonymous | no |
| `target` | pseudonymous | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | no | retain_pseudonymous | no |
| `ua` | pii | audit_and_compliance | years_1 | yes | retain_pseudonymous | no |

Notes:

- `actorId`: Pseudonymous. Survives erasure so the trail stays attributable.
- `entryHash`: H(prev_hash || canonical(entry)). Verified on a schedule (4.13.3).
- `ip`: Retained under legal obligation, so erasure does not clear it (Art.17(3)(b)).
- `outboxSeq`: The outbox row this entry was relayed from, and what makes a replay a no-op instead of a duplicate. Null on an entry with no outbox event behind it.
- `prevHash`: Hash of the preceding entry for this project. Genesis is 64 zeroes.
- `projectId`: Tenant discriminator. Enforced by the repository layer.
- `seq`: Total order across every partition, from one cluster sequence. The chain needs it: created_at ties at millisecond precision, and two entries in the same millisecond would leave the project's tip ambiguous and fork the chain (PROJECT.md 4.13.3).

| `updatedBy` | operational | audit_and_compliance | project_lifetime | no | not_applicable | no |

Notes:

- `autoTopUpAmountCents`: How much to add. Below the threshold it would fire on itself.
- `autoTopUpDailyLimit`: Attempts allowed in any rolling day. Set by support, never over the wire.
- `autoTopUpFailures`: Consecutive automatic charges that did not succeed. A success resets it.
- `autoTopUpLastAttemptAt`: When the rule last opened a charge, which is what spaces the next one out.
- `autoTopUpMethodId`: Which card it charges. Null falls back to the default, and the panel says so.
- `autoTopUpSuspendedAt`: Set when charging again cannot help. Cleared only by a person saving the rule.
- `autoTopUpSuspendedReason`: AutoTopUpSuspension: what the person who clears it has to fix first.
- `autoTopUpThresholdCents`: Charge when the spendable balance falls below this.
- `billingMode`: BillingMode. Set by Idenzy staff only, with a reason in operator_actions (ADR-0019).
- `currency`: Set at the provider and not from here. One currency per account.
- `invoiceEmail`: Where an invoiced organisation's invoices are sent. Staff-set with the mode.
- `invoiceTermsDays`: Net terms for an invoiced organisation. Staff-set; 14 unless agreed otherwise.
- `orgId`: Organisation discriminator. Enforced by the repository layer.
- `spendAlertSentForMonth`: The month already alerted on, so a threshold crossed once is not mailed hourly.
- `spendAlertThresholdCents`: An alert and never a cap. Authentication does not stop (5.1).

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

Notes:

- `amountCents`: What it was worth when granted. Never changes, which is what makes it auditable.
- `expiresAt`: Null says it does not expire, which is the truth about purchased credit.
- `kind`: CreditKind. Purchased credit does not expire; promotional credit does.
- `note`: Why it exists, in the words the wallet screen shows: a top-up, a trial, a credit.
- `orgId`: Organisation discriminator. Enforced by the repository layer.
- `remainingCents`: What is left. Drawn down by the metering job, never below zero or above amount.
- `topUpId`: The purchase that created it. Null on a grant nobody paid for.

Notes:

- `bouncedHard`: Permanent bounces. These suppress the address as well as counting here.
- `bouncedSoft`: Transient and undetermined. They suppress nothing and still count towards our rate at AWS.
- `day`: UTC day the event was received, not the day the message was sent.
- `projectId`: Tenant discriminator. Enforced by the repository layer.
- `rejected`: SES refused it outright, usually for a virus or an address on its account suppression list.
- `sent`: SES accepted it. The denominator every rate on this row is over.

Notes:

- `deletedAt`: Tombstone marker. The row survives erasure with its personal columns cleared.
- `id`: Survives erasure so the audit trail keeps a stable pseudonymous subject.
- `metadataPrivate`: Readable only with a secret key. Never returned to a client SDK.
- `metadataPublic`: Customer-controlled. Assume it holds personal data, because it usually does.
- `passwordAlgoVersion`: Lets a hash be upgraded transparently on next login (PROJECT.md 4.5).
- `projectId`: Tenant discriminator. Enforced by the repository layer.

Notes:

- `backupEligible`: The signed BE flag. Fixed for the credential's life: an authenticator that changes it is not the one we registered.
- `backupState`: The signed BS flag, which does move: an eligible credential is backed up later, not at registration.
- `lastUsedAt`: Advanced on every successful assertion, so the owner can tell which passkey is stale.
- `name`: User-chosen label, such as the name of a phone.
- `projectId`: Tenant discriminator. Enforced by the repository layer.
- `signCount`: A decrease suggests a cloned authenticator and is a security signal.
